questions.q: What problem does a software catalog solve that a wiki page describing the same services usually fails at?
options: It keeps the inventory live and queryable, tied to real entities instead of documentation that silently goes stale
It replaces the need for any CI/CD pipeline entirely
It encrypts service metadata so only admins can view it
It automatically rewrites a service's business logic
questions.explain: A wiki page can go stale with nobody noticing. A catalog entity like a Backstage catalog-info.yaml is a live, structured record ingested by the platform, so a missing or wrong owner field is immediately visible rather than silently rotting.

questions.q: In Backstage's catalog, what does a catalog-info.yaml file with kind: Component actually represent?
options: A one-time snapshot of a CI pipeline's last run
An entity descriptor registering that service in the catalog, with its owner, lifecycle, and dependencies
A Kubernetes Deployment manifest used to run the service
A backup copy of the service's source code
questions.explain: The YAML entity descriptor, usually committed in the service's own repo, is what makes the service real to the catalog -- searchable, owned by a real team, and part of a dependency graph.

questions.q: What does a Backstage software template (the Scaffolder) actually do when a developer fills out its form?
options: It only validates that the developer's chosen service name is not already taken
It deletes the developer's existing repository and starts over
It generates a new, correctly wired-up component -- CI/CD, monitoring, infra -- instead of the developer copying and adapting an existing repo by hand
It schedules a manual review meeting before any code can be written
questions.explain: A software template scaffolds a brand-new service from a templated source tree with the pipeline, monitoring, and infrastructure already connected, replacing ad hoc copy-paste-and-strip-out onboarding.

questions.q: In the example template.yaml, what does the final 'register' step accomplish, and why does it matter?
options: It deploys the new service straight to production without a pipeline
It is purely cosmetic and has no effect on the catalog
It requests a code review from the owning team's manager
It calls catalog:register so the newly scaffolded service is automatically added to the catalog, closing the loop between creation and inventory
questions.explain: Without an automatic register step, a team could scaffold a working service that never shows up in the org-wide catalog -- recreating the exact invisible-sprawl problem the catalog exists to prevent.

questions.q: Why do the catalog and software templates need each other to actually work, according to this lesson?
options: The catalog is only useful if new services reliably appear in it, and templates that don't register their output just create more invisible sprawl -- wired together, every new service is visible with a real owner from the start
A catalog without templates is pointless unless it also replaces version control
Templates need the catalog only to check billing codes before provisioning
They do not actually depend on each other; either one alone fully solves the discovery problem
questions.explain: The catalog depends on templates to keep it populated with accurate data, and templates depend on the catalog to make what they create discoverable -- each is incomplete without the other.
